question: For weekly-sales data, I need an analysis of our sales performance around mid-June for the years 2018, 2019, and 2020. Specifically, calculate the percentage change in sales between the four weeks leading up to June 15 and the four weeks following June 15 for each year.
sql:
WITH weekly_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        calendar_year,
        week_date,
        SUM(sales) as total_sales
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales 
    WHERE calendar_year IN (2018, 2019, 2020)
    GROUP BY calendar_year, week_date
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        calendar_year,
        week_date,
        total_sales,
        CAST(week_date AS DATE) - CAST(calendar_year || '-06-15' AS DATE) as day_diff,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY calendar_year ORDER BY CAST(week_date AS DATE) - CAST(calendar_year || '-06-15' AS DATE)) as rn
    FROM weekly_totals
)
SELECT 
    calendar_year,
    SUM(CASE WHEN rn BETWEEN 9 AND 12 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) as pre_sales,
    SUM(CASE WHEN rn BETWEEN 13 AND 16 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) as post_sales,
    ROUND(1.0 * (SUM(CASE WHEN rn BETWEEN 13 AND 16 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN rn BETWEEN 9 AND 12 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END)) / SUM(CASE WHEN rn BETWEEN 9 AND 12 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) * 100, 2) as pct_change
FROM ranked
GROUP BY calendar_year
ORDER BY calendar_year
